diagrams.title: **Stateless vs memory-enabled
diagrams.caption: **Stateless vs memory-enabled.** On the left, each new conversation is a stranger. On the right, the agent writes what's useful during one conversation and reads it back in the next.

diagrams.title: **Short-term and long-term, and three kinds of long-term
diagrams.caption: **Short-term and long-term, and three kinds of long-term.** Everything the agent experiences is processed into memory, and everything in memory exists to be retrieved when the agent needs to decide or respond.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 400" aria-label="Types of agent memory. Agent experiences (observations, interactions, tasks and actions) go into memory processing. Processing feeds short-term memory (recent events, temporary context) and long-term memory, which has three kinds: episodic (experiences and events), procedural (skills and how-to) and semantic (facts and concepts). diagrams.title: **Experienced, done, known
diagrams.caption: **Experienced, done, known.** Episodic memory captures what the agent has lived through, procedural memory how it does things, semantic memory what it knows.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 320" aria-label="Three types of long-term memory. Episodic: personal experiences and specific events, for example your trip to Goa or last month's refund issue. Procedural: skills and routines, how to get things done, for example riding a bike or filing an expense claim. Semantic: general knowledge, facts, definitions and rules, for example Delhi is India's capital, dogs are mammals." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
        <rect x="20" y="20" width="340" height="280" rx="18" class="brain" style="fill:#FFF1CC;stroke:#B07600;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
